game.title: Urn of unknown mix
game.description: An urn holds 10 balls, each red or blue. Each ball was independently painted red with probability 0.6. 4 balls are drawn without replacement. Revealed draws show 1 for red and 0 for blue.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of red balls originally in the urn.

info.raw:
The urn's red-ball count follows a Binomial(10, 0.6) prior, so the mean is 6 and the standard deviation is about 1.55. That makes the public fair value 6.

The share of informed traders is unknown; averaged over the three possibilities it is about 0.48. That is high enough that a tight quote loses money:

- **Ask at 6.6:** expected profit per quote is about −0.09. Informed traders buy whenever the value is 7 or more, which happens 38% of the time.
- **Ask from about 7.5 to 8.5:** expected profit per quote is roughly zero.

I'll quote wide and roughly symmetric around 6, at 4.2 / 7.8. This limits losses to informed traders while still earning from noise traders. Any trades will also tell me something about how many traders are informed.

{"bid": 4.2, "ask": 7.8}

With no reveals yet, fair value is the prior mean: 10 × 0.6 = 6, with standard deviation about 1.55. The quote of 4.2 / 7.8 drew no trade, which hints slightly that the value is mid-range but barely changes the estimate.

On the ask side, at 7.2:
- **Informed buyers:** they buy only when the value is 8 or more. My expected loss to them is about 0.19 per quote.
- **Noise buyers:** they buy with about 14% probability, and I gain about 1.2 each time, so about 0.17 per quote.

The bid side at 4.8 is roughly symmetric. With alpha averaging about 0.48, quoting 6 ± 1.2 roughly breaks even. Getting some trades also helps me learn alpha.

{"bid": 4.8, "ask": 7.2}

The two revealed red draws raise fair value to **6.8**. Given those two draws, the other 8 balls are still each red with probability 0.6, so the value is 2 plus a Binomial(8, 0.6) count. That gives a mean of 6.8 and a standard deviation of about 1.39, with integer outcomes from 2 to 10.

The informed share (alpha) is undisclosed, so I priced each side at its expected value of about 0.48. For each candidate price I compared two things:
- **Gain from noise traders:** valuation is fair value plus noise with standard deviation 1.1.
- **Loss to informed traders:** they trade whenever the true value lies outside my quote.

**Ask side:**

| Ask | Approx. edge per quote |
|---|---|
| 7.5 | -0.04 (too much informed loss when the value is 8–10) |
| 8.0 | +0.027 |
| 8.1 | +0.026 |
| 8.5 | +0.02 |

An ask of 8.0 is best. An informed trader only buys if the value is strictly above 8, i.e. 9 or 10.

**Bid side:**

| Bid | Approx. edge per quote |
|---|---|
| 6.0 | negative |
| 5.5 | +0.01 |
| 5.1 | +0.028 |
| 5.0 | +0.02 |

A bid of about 5.1–5.2 is best. Below 6, an informed trader only sells when the value is 5 or lower.

I'll quote a fairly wide but positive-edge market.

{"bid": 5.2, "ask": 8.0}

The contract's value is the number of red balls, which follows Binomial(10, 0.6). That gives a mean of 6 and a standard deviation of about 1.55. Nothing is revealed yet, so the fair value is 6.

**What round 1 told me:** No trades happened in round 1, but that says little about alpha. The value settled at 6, inside my quotes, so an informed counterparty would not have traded anyway.

**Choosing the spread:** I averaged over the possible alpha values, giving an expected alpha of about 0.48. For each candidate price I compared expected gain from noise traders against expected loss to informed traders:

| Quote | Gain from noise traders | Loss to informed traders | Net per quote |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ask 7.0 | 0.18 | 0.22 | about −0.01 |
| Ask 7.9 | 0.08 | 0.07 | about +0.008 |
| Ask 8.0 | 0.069 | 0.052 | about +0.011 (best) |
| Ask 8.5 | 0.029 | 0.029 | about 0 |
| Bid 4.0 | 0.069 | 0.069 | about +0.002 |
| Bid 3.9 | 0.059 | 0.064 | about 0 |

- At an ask of 8.0, an informed trader only buys when the value is 9 or 10, since it must be strictly above the ask.
- The bid side is not quite symmetric because the prior leans towards red. A bid of 4.0 is about break-even and slightly better than 3.9.
- Any trades also help me learn alpha.

{"bid": 4.0, "ask": 8.0}

No-trade quotes so far tell me little about alpha (the share of informed counterparties). Quoting a bit tighter has some learning value for later rounds, and its expected profit is roughly break-even.

- **Value before any reveal:** red balls ~ Bin(10, 0.6), so the mean is 6 and the standard deviation is about 1.55.
- **Quote checked:** 4.5 bid / 7.5 ask.
- **Noise traders:** expected profit is about 0.26 per noise counterparty.
- **Informed traders:** expected loss is about 0.29 per informed counterparty.
- **Net:** with alpha unknown (average about 0.48), these roughly cancel.

{"bid": 4.5, "ask": 7.5}

Fair value is 5.8. I'd quote 4.1 to buy and 7.1 to sell. Both sides are skewed wide because I don't know alpha.

**Fair value.** The draws were blue then red, so 1 red ball is confirmed. The other 8 balls are each red with probability 0.6. That gives an expected count of 1 + 8 × 0.6 = 5.8. The settlement value V is 1 plus a Binomial(8, 0.6) count:

| V | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P | 0.23 | 0.28 | 0.21 | 0.09 | 0.02 |

**Alpha estimate.** We've had no trades so far, but our quotes were wide, so that tells us little. I keep the prior mean of about 0.48.

**Choosing each side.** For each candidate price I compared:
- Noise-trader profit: (1 − alpha) × P(noise crosses my price) × my edge over 5.8.
- Informed-trader loss: alpha × the expected amount by which V is beyond my price.

| Side | Price | Noise profit | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ask | 6.9 | 0.091 | 0.074 | +0.017 |
| Ask | 7.1 | 0.080 | 0.054 | +0.026 |
| Ask | 7.5 | 0.054 | 0.034 | +0.02 |
| Bid | 3.9 | 0.042 | 0.026 | +0.016 |
| Bid | 4.1 | 0.054 | 0.037 | +0.017 |
| Bid | 4.5 | 0.080 | 0.070 | +0.01 |

The ask at 7.1 sits just above the 7 settlement outcome. The bid at 4.1 sits just above 4, so I only lose to informed sellers when V is 4 or lower. If alpha turns out to be 0.9, both sides lose money on average. Averaged over the possible alphas, both are slightly positive, and any trades will also tell us something about alpha.

{"bid": 4.1, "ask": 7.1}

Fair value is about 5.8, and I'm quoting a bid of 4.0 and an ask of 7.0.

**Fair value.** One of the two revealed draws is red. Each of the other 8 balls is still red with probability 0.6, independently. So the settlement value is 1 + Binomial(8, 0.6). Its mean is 1 + 4.8 = 5.8 and its standard deviation is about 1.39.

**Uncertainty about alpha.** There have been no trades yet, so I can't tell how many counterparties are informed. I treat alpha as about 0.5.

**Ask.** An informed trader buys at 7.0 only if the value is 8 or more, which has probability about 0.11. The expected loss to informed traders is about 0.12. The expected gain from noise traders buying is about 0.17. Weighted by alpha, this gives a small positive edge of about +0.03 per quote. An ask of 7.0 is about as good as anything in the 7.0–7.9 range.

**Bid.** An informed trader sells at 4.0 only if the value is 3 or less, which has probability about 0.05. The expected loss to informed traders is about 0.06. The expected gain from noise traders selling is about 0.09. That gives a small positive edge of about +0.02 per quote. Bids at 4.5 or higher lose too much to informed sellers when the value is 4.

{"bid": 4.0, "ask": 7.0}

The prior for the number of red balls is Binomial(10, 0.6), so the fair value is 6. Nothing has been revealed this round. No trades have happened yet, so nothing has shown how often counterparties are informed. My prior average for that share (alpha) is still about 0.48.

**Ask side**
- An informed buyer costs me E[(V − ask)⁺], the expected amount by which the true value exceeds my ask.
- A noise buyer earns me (ask − 6) times the chance its valuation lands above my ask.
- At 7.5 the two roughly cancel.
- At 8.1 the expected informed loss is about 0.023 per quote and the noise gain is about 0.030, so it comes out slightly positive.

**Bid side**
- The distribution has a heavier tail toward low values, so the bid sits a bit further from fair value.
- At 4.1 the edge is about zero (0.041 against 0.041).
- At 3.9 it is still roughly break-even (0.030 against 0.030), with a small cushion if informed traders turn out to be common.

I'll quote a wide spread for now. A trade at these prices would also tell me something about alpha.

{"bid": 3.9, "ask": 8.1}

Quoting 4.0 / 8.0 for a small positive expected edge on each side.

**Value of the contract.** Nothing is revealed yet this round, so the number of red balls follows Binomial(10, 0.6). Its mean is 6 and its standard deviation is about 1.55. The noise traders' valuations centre on 6 with noise of standard deviation 1.1.

**Informed share (alpha).** It is unknown. No trades have happened yet, which tells me little, so I use the average of the three possible values, about 0.48.

**Ask side** (expected profit per quote):

| Ask | Gain from noise buyers | Loss to informed buyers | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7.5 | 0.52 × 0.129 | 0.48 × 0.136 | ≈ 0 |
| 7.9 | 0.52 × 0.080 | 0.48 × 0.069 | ≈ +0.008 |
| 8.0 | 0.52 × 0.069 | 0.48 × 0.052 | ≈ +0.011 |

At 8.0, informed traders only buy when the urn holds 9 or 10 red balls.

**Bid side:**

| Bid | Gain from noise sellers | Loss to informed sellers | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | 0.52 × 0.080 | 0.48 × 0.085 | ≈ 0 |
| 4.0 | 0.52 × 0.069 | 0.48 × 0.069 | ≈ +0.003 |

At 4.0, informed traders only sell when the urn holds 3 or fewer red balls.

{"bid": 4.0, "ask": 8.0}

Quoting bid 4.3, ask 7.1: slightly asymmetric around the fair value, because the risk from informed traders is lopsided.

**Fair value.** One red and one blue have been drawn, and each of the other 8 balls is red with probability 0.6. So the expected count is 1 + 8 × 0.6 = 5.8, with a standard deviation of about 1.4.

**How likely informed traders are.** In round 2 the value was 4. My bid was 4.5 and then 4.1, so an informed trader would have sold to me both times, and nobody traded. That is strong evidence against alpha = 0.9. The other quotes had no trades either, which fits informed traders who saw nothing worth trading. After that, alpha = 0.05 and alpha = 0.5 are roughly equally likely.

**Choosing the spread.** I compared, for each side, the profit from noise traders against the loss to informed traders, for alpha = 0.05 and alpha = 0.5:
- **Bid side:** informed traders hurt more here because the value distribution has more weight below the fair value. A bid of 4.3 still has positive expected profit when alpha = 0.5.
- **Ask side:** an ask of 7.1 gives slightly positive expected profit when alpha = 0.5 and a good profit when alpha = 0.05.

{"bid": 4.3, "ask": 7.1}

Fair value is about 5.8, and I'm quoting a symmetric spread of 4.8 bid / 6.8 ask around it.

- **Fair value:** one red and one blue are known. Each of the other 8 balls is red with probability 0.6, so the expected count is 1 + 8 × 0.6 = 5.8. The standard deviation is about 1.39.

That pushes the estimate toward low alpha, roughly 78% on 0.05 and 22% on 0.5. The effective alpha is about 0.15.
- **Ask:** I traded off noise-trader profit (noise has standard deviation 1.1 around 5.8) against expected losses to informed buyers. The expected profit peaks around 6.8, at about +0.13 per quote.

{"bid": 4.8, "ask": 6.8}

Quoting bid 4.0 and ask 8.0, about 2 either side of the prior fair value of 6.

**Prior fair value.** Nothing is revealed yet, so the number of red balls follows a Binomial(10, 0.6) distribution. Its mean is 6 and its standard deviation is about 1.55.

**What we know about alpha.** There have been no trades in the first three rounds. My quotes were wide, so this tells us little. I treat the chance of an informed counterparty as roughly the prior average, about 0.48.

- At 4.0 it is about +0.002.

A trade would also tell me something about alpha, which is worth a little extra.

{"bid": 4.0, "ask": 8.0}

With no trades so far, the informed-trader rate is probably low, so I'll tighten to about 1 point on each side of the fair value of 6.

- **Fair value:** the number of red balls is Binomial(10, 0.6), so it has mean 6 and standard deviation about 1.55.

An informed counterparty would have sold to me at either quote, and neither did. That strongly favours alpha = 0.05 (posterior about 0.78) over 0.5 (about 0.21) and 0.9 (about 0.01). |---|---|---|---|

- **Informed share (alpha):** in round 2, quote 3, an informed trader would have sold at my 4.1 bid against a value of 4, and nobody did. That is strong evidence against alpha = 0.9. My rough posterior is about 0.45 / 0.42 / 0.13 for alpha = 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9.
